_comment: 🧩️ This subset's own contribution to the repository test platform: the exhaustive BinaryMutation vocabulary for stdio.binary raw/✳️any, and the recorded no-oracle decision that backs it. A raw byte buffer has no format, so there is nothing for a third-party library to be authoritative about — no crate was hunted for and none is registered. See the decision's own rationale below.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: A raw byte buffer carries no format — it is bytes, full stop. There is no grammar for a third-party library to parse, no independent reader to project both sides through, and no credible reference WRITER either: agreeing or disagreeing with some arbitrary crate would measure that crate's own opinion of what 'a buffer' is, not a defect in this subset. The specification IS the mutation vocabulary itself (`BinaryMutation`'s five variants and their documented offset/remove_len contract in `../🧬️schema/🧬️mutations/🦀️.rs`), so the evidence is the specification vectors below plus the inverse law as a metamorphic property — both discharged by this module's own independently written splice/append/truncate implementation (`../🦀️oracle.rs`), which never touches the subject's `BinaryDiff`/`apply_binary_mutation`. [Narrowed 2026-09-02, ticket 26/09/02/SEPARATE-ARTIFACT-STANDARD-SUBSET-IMPLEMENTATIONS-AND-FIXTURE-TEST-EVERY-MUTATION shard D2: capabilities emptied because a real mutationManifest now requires a qualifying third-party oracle for this exact capability, and noOracleMisuseBreaches correctly refuses to let a recorded decision paper over a real runtime requirement (per shard A10's precedent for mathematical/sequence/draw) -- the honest state is a visible missing-external-oracle gap, not a hidden one. Rationale above is kept for the record: it still explains why no third-party library is credible for this domain, which is exactly why the gap is expected to stay open rather than be filled.]
